# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — empty-seed init: code-enforce payment/baggage, surface exact $, execute-on-confirm
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: `_autocorrect_payment_amounts` (cluster A — payment sum mismatch) fires only on sum≠total; single method→pays total, multi with one credit card→cc absorbs remainder; then re-sync `payment_history` (latent hashed-field bug).
  - tools.py `_normalize_payment_dicts` in `book_reservation` (cluster B — malformed `{'type','id'}` dicts): id→payment_id, drop type/source, default amount.
  - tools.py book/cancel/update_* enriched return with `payment_summary` exact-$ string (cluster C — COMMUNICATE omission); returns not hashed ⇒ DB-safe.
  - tools.py `_recompute_nonfree_baggages` in `book_reservation` + `update_reservation_baggages`, plus `if total_price>0` payment guard (cluster D — baggage miscount + spurious $50).
  - policy.md §1–§4 + softness clause (clusters A/C/E): execute-on-confirm SAME turn, trust tool for amounts/baggage, state exact $, pull DOB from profile.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - A: task 25 (gift128+cc171 for 375) and 23 (four methods 871 for 946) stop raising → write happens on first confirm → no 2nd-round ###STOP###. Verified gold-exact on live DB; no-op on correct amounts so passing bookings untouched.
  - B: task 8/23/25 malformed dicts no longer die on validation. Verified: task 8 cert dict → stored [cert 348]=gold. Well-formed dicts unchanged.
  - C: task 11 (passing) proves the need; enriched return gives weak model the exact figure to echo. Only adds a field; task 11 path unchanged.
  - D: task 12 (gold/economy/2pax, 1 bag) → nonfree 0, no $50 = gold. No-op when caller correct.
  - E: reinforces task 11's correct execute-on-confirm; softness clause keeps agent reward-maximizing.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration (LEDGER/JOURNAL/rejected.jsonl all empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: multi-reservation split (23), incomplete multi-write where update_flights is skipped (22), wrong-FLIGHT selection (8/25 flaky), over-eager transfer (40). All are model reasoning/selection with no general code guard; addressed only indirectly via policy. Designs tried: none in code (a flight/subset literal guard would overfit).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency not a declared objective here (reward = DB×COMMUNICATE). Auto-correct + normalization still cut round-trips (fewer error-retry loops → less ###STOP### exposure), a reliability win not a declared-cost win. Did not run detect_loop_patterns.py.
- Focus next iteration: if ACCEPTED, read RESULT to see which of 25/23/12/8 moved; then target the reasoning clusters (22 incomplete multi-write, 23 split) with prose worked-examples, since code can't safely encode them. If REJECTED, bisect: the two highest-confidence, gold-verified levers are the payment auto-correct (A) and baggage recompute (D) — keep those, drop the enriched-return (C) first if a passing task regressed (it is the widest blast radius).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.300 Δ=-0.100 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 12, 19, 25, 37, 8} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — no task that was passing under the parent regressed: this batch did not clear the gate's threshold, it did not do damage. So the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — re-measure with more trials in ONE evaluation, or make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the `fixed` tasks above as your starting point; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers.
<!-- cand_0001: rejected val=0.300 Δ=-0.100 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — keep cand_0001's gold-verified code; drop its refuted/wide edits; add cancel-flown guard + reservation/policy clarifications
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - tools.py `book_reservation` (+helpers `_to_payment`, `_autocorrect_payment_amounts`): normalize malformed `{id/type}` payment dicts, auto-correct amounts when sum≠total (single pays total; else the one credit card absorbs the remainder), re-sync `payment_history`+recomputed `nonfree_baggages` before persist (clusters B payment, C baggage).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages`: recompute `nonfree=max(0,total−FREE[membership][cabin]×npax)` and charge only when `total_price>0` (cluster C).
  - tools.py `cancel_reservation`: NEW discriminating guard — refuse if any flight segment is already flown (`status in {flying,landed}`) (cluster D, task 37 extra forbidden cancel of NQNU5R).
  - policy.md "Operating notes" §1–§6 + softness clause: route-match the reservation / never act on the first-listed or a guessed id (§1), basic-economy CAN change cabin/upgrade though its flights are locked (§2), don't transfer/refuse an in-policy action (§3), state the exact charged/refunded $ (§4, COMMUNICATE), DOB from profile (§5), trust the tools for amounts/baggage (§6) (clusters A, E, and task 40).
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - B/C book_reservation: task 25 (gift128+cc171→247) and malformed-dict (cert 348) now write on first confirm; task 12/17/22 nonfree→gold. Verified gold-exact AND no-op on correct input on live DB; task 11 is not a booking so unaffected.
  - C update_baggages: within-allowance change no longer fails on an unneeded payment_id and never appends a spurious $50; no-op when caller already correct.
  - D cancel guard: blocks exactly the forbidden NQNU5R cancel in task 37 t2 → its DB then matches gold (only the M20IZO upgrade). Verified future cancels (Z7GOZK task19, K1NW8N task23) still succeed.
  - A/E policy: fixes the decoy-reservation trap (17,22 grab UM3OG5 instead of FQ8APE) and the wrong "basic economy can't be modified" refusal (22 t0 found FQ8APE then refused the allowed upgrade). Reinforces task 11's already-correct exact-$ statement; no rule flips a passing decision.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 REJECTED (−0.100, broke={} fixed={}). I KEPT its two highest-confidence gold-verified levers (payment auto-correct, baggage recompute) as the RESULT advised, and DID NOT re-try its two widest-blast-radius edits: (1) the dict-return `payment_summary` enrichment — low COMMUNICATE coverage (only tasks 11 & 23 have non-empty communicate_info) and re-read every turn; (2) the prose "execute-on-confirm same-turn" anti-STALL rule.
- Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test): prose anti-STALL "act after confirming / same turn" (cand_0001 §1; tools SKILL marks it refuted for the narrated-without-action class). Also: task 37 is NOT a COMMUNICATE failure — it is an extra forbidden cancel (DB); `'HATHAT'`-style ids are tool-returned, not hallucinated.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: STALL/narrated-without-action (19 t1, 22 t0, 25 t2) — prose refuted and a composite-write+remove is unsafe here because cancel/update MUST stay refusable (task 37 forbidden cancel, basic-economy flight-change refusal); design a SAFE composite only. Multi-reservation split (23) and wrong-flight selection (8,23) — model/user-sim selection, no general guard.
- Plateau signal: one reject so far (cand_0001). Lever switch this round = from "one big noisy batch incl. a wide dict-return" to "focused, strictly-no-op-on-correct code guards (incl. a NEW cancel-flown guard) + targeted policy clarifications", raising signal-to-noise and adding a clean bounded win (task 37).

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## val-split scoring facts (verified against tau2 source, this run)
- Only tasks **11** (`['5244']`, passing) and **23** (`['327','1000','1286']`) have non-empty `communicate_info`. Every other val task has `communicate_info=[]`, so COMMUNICATE is trivially 1.0 for them and their failures are pure DB. ⇒ a broad COMMUNICATE enrichment (dict-return) has LOW coverage on this split; a narrow policy "state the exact $" contract is enough.
- **Tasks 17 and 22 are the SAME scenario** (user omar_rossi_1241, NY→Chicago = FQ8APE EWR→ORD): change passenger to self + upgrade basic_economy→economy + add 3 bags, pay by gift card. Gold = 3 writes on FQ8APE. Decoy reservation UM3OG5 is SEA↔DFW. The agent's dominant error is acting on UM3OG5 (first-listed) and/or refusing the upgrade as "basic economy can't be modified" (it CAN change cabin).
- **Task 37 t2 fails on DB (an EXTRA forbidden cancel of NQNU5R, both flights `landed`/flown), NOT on COMMUNICATE.** Guarding `cancel_reservation` to refuse a flown-segment reservation removes the extra write; the required M20IZO upgrade is already correct.
- `'HATHAT'`/`'HATHAU'` reservation ids are the mock `book_reservation`'s fixed returned ids, NOT hallucinations.

## What didn't (confirmed by cand_0001 RESULT: rejected −0.100, broke={} fixed={})
- A single large batch that included a wide dict-return enrichment + a prose "execute-on-confirm same-turn" anti-STALL rule landed within noise (SE=0.1, n=10). Nothing measurably broke or fixed. Lesson: favour edits that are strictly no-op on correct input (fire-only-on-error guards) to raise signal-to-noise on a noisy 10-task gate.

## Promising but not yet tried
- A SAFE composite write for the STALL cluster limited to an unambiguous single-action path (e.g. a confirm+cancel for a clearly-eligible reservation), without removing the refusable primitives.
- Turning policy §1 (route-match) into a `get_all_reservation_details(user_id)` loop/read tool if 17/22 stay flaky under the prose rule.

## task 11 COMMUNICATE — the refund IS in the return; the model quotes a stale estimate (cand_0003, pending RESULT)
- Verified live: `update_reservation_flights` on task 11's downgrade already returns `payment_history` summing to **-5244**; the 2/3 failing trials score 0 because the model states its pre-confirmation arithmetic ($1748 = per-passenger figure, forgot ×3 passengers) instead of reading the return. So this is a READ-THE-RETURN failure, not a compute failure.
- Lever shipped: enrich the return with `payment_summary` = exact amount + copy-ready sentence + "use THIS figure, not your estimate", and policy §4 tells the weak model to prefer it over its own math with the ×N worked example. DB byte-identical (returns not hashed) ⇒ zero regression risk on passing 12/17/22. (Awaiting RESULT to confirm it moves task 11.)

## agent-uncontrollable USER_STOP (cand_0003)
- Tasks 19 t1 and 40 t1 end with the user-sim's confirmation message itself carrying `###STOP###` — the episode terminates before the agent gets an action turn. These are NOT narrate-without-action and have NO agent-side prompt/tool lever. Confirmed from traces across iterations; do not spend a lever on them.

## reading RESULT lines: within-noise ≠ regressed (cand_0003)
- cand_0001 `rejected broke={} fixed={}` meant within-noise, and its own RESULT said "POWER or SIZE, not a redesign." The correct response to a within-noise lever you believe in is to make it BIGGER/sharper on a known-good base, not to drop it. cand_0003 did exactly that with the exact-$ enrichment (dropped in cand_0002 as "low coverage") — re-added sharper on top of the accepted champion.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first)
- Strategy tried: diagnosed the 10-task val split directly, then shipped FIVE edit classes in one candidate (in-body auto-correct, dict normalization, arithmetic recompute, enriched returns, policy rules) rather than one timid lever. Every code lever was replayed on the exact failing-trace arguments against the LIVE airline DB and shown gold-exact before shipping — this is the decisive quality gate for a DB-hashed benchmark where you cannot run the eval yourself.
- Key leverage insight: reward = DB × COMMUNICATE, and the dominant zero-score cause is NOT wrong DB logic but (a) the write never executing because an error forces a 2nd confirmation that the user-sim ends with ###STOP###, and (b) a correct DB with the dollar figure never spoken. So the highest-leverage code move is to make the FIRST write succeed (auto-correct amounts/format/baggage in-body) and the highest-leverage comms move is to hand the weak model the exact $ in the return.
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (iteration 1).
- What to try next: let the gate tell us which levers moved; reserve prose worked-examples for the reasoning clusters (multi-write completeness, multi-reservation split) that code cannot safely encode.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: on a noisy gate (SE=0.1, n=10) where cand_0001's big batch landed within noise (LEDGER row 1, rejected −0.100), switch from "throw everything" to "maximize signal-to-noise": ship only edits that are strictly no-op on correct input (fire-only-on-error code guards) plus a clean bounded new win (cancel-flown guard, task 37) and targeted policy clarifications for the biggest cluster (decoy reservation 17/22). Dropped cand_0001's two widest/refuted edits (dict-return enrichment, prose same-turn anti-STALL).
- Used a read-only diagnosis subagent across all 30 trajectories FIRST — it corrected two intake hypotheses (task 37 = extra forbidden cancel not COMMUNICATE; `'HATHAT'` ids are tool-returned). Diagnosing before editing prevented two wasted levers.
- Every code lever replayed on the exact failing-trace args against the live DB and shown gold-exact + no-op-on-correct before shipping — the decisive quality gate when you can't run the eval yourself.
- Plateau/stall signal: STALL/narrated-without-action remains the one systemic cluster with no safe lever found yet (prose refuted, composite unsafe here). If this iteration is also flat, the next move is a narrowly-scoped safe composite, not another prose rule.
- What to try next: gate-driven — keep the four code guards (strictly safe), and treat the policy prose block as the swing factor to trim if broke={} recurs.

## Iteration cand_0003 (LAST of run, 3/3)
- Strategy tried: build ADDITIVELY on the accepted champion cand_0002 rather than re-batching. Kept all four verified code guards + policy §1–§6 verbatim, and added only strictly-no-op surface: a DB-safe `payment_summary` return key (returns are not hashed) plus three prose decision rules. Rationale: cand_0002 cleared the noisy gate (+0.217) by raising signal-to-noise; the way to not lose that is to not perturb any already-correct decision — a new key and STOP-only rules change no passing DB state.
- Re-interpreted a prior "dropped" lever correctly: cand_0001's dict-return enrichment was dropped in cand_0002 as "low coverage", but its RESULT was broke={}/fixed={} = within-noise, NOT a regression. cand_0001's own RESULT said "the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign." So I did not abandon it — I made it SHARPER (exact copy-ready directive + §4 telling the weak model to prefer the returned figure over its own estimate, with the ×N-passengers worked example that is exactly task 11's failure mode). Meta-lesson: distinguish "within-noise, make it bigger" from "regressed, redesign" when reading RESULT lines — they look similar (both broke={}) but call for opposite moves.
- Plateau/stall signal: the two remaining DB-zero clusters are now cleanly characterised as UN-leverable from the agent side on this split — (a) uncontrollable USER_STOP (simulator ends the episode in the user's confirmation turn), (b) model flight/passenger selection and multi-reservation split (reasoning, not encodable without overfitting). This is the real ceiling of prompt+tools edits on this 10-task val split; further gains need either eval-side (more trials to de-noise) or a benchmark-side fix to the USER_STOP bundling, not another capability edit.
- What to try next run: if the objective ever adds cost/latency, run detect_loop_patterns.py (free) for a bulk-tool opportunity. For reward, the only untried safe lever is a narrowly-scoped confirm+write composite for the unambiguous single-action path — design it so cancel/update stay refusable (cancel-flown guard, basic-economy flight-change) so it cannot defeat the task-37-class guards.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From run suite_smoke_tau2_proj (cand_0003, last iteration)
- **RESULT lines should distinguish "within-noise" from "regressed".** cand_0001's RESULT read `rejected · broke={} · unresolved={...}` and the prose correctly explained "no task regressed; the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign." That nuance is gold, but it lives only in free-text; the structured fields (`broke`/`fixed`/`unresolved`) look identical to a true regression's. Suggestion: add an explicit machine-readable verdict tag like `signal=within_noise | regressed | improved` to the RESULT stamp so an optimizer does not mistakenly abandon a within-noise lever (I nearly dropped the exact-$ enrichment for that reason). This is a recurring foot-gun on noisy small-split gates (SE≈0.1, n=10).
- **Surface which tasks have non-empty `communicate_info` up front.** A large chunk of iteration-1 diagnosis time went into discovering (via tau2 source) that only 2 of 10 val tasks score COMMUNICATE at all; the rest are pure-DB. A one-line per-task breakdown (`db_only` vs `db+communicate`, and the gold `communicate_info` literals) in the task intake would let the optimizer size COMMUNICATE-vs-DB levers immediately instead of reverse-engineering the scorer.
- **Flag uncontrollable USER_STOP tasks.** Tasks 19 t1 / 40 t1 are unwinnable from the agent side because the user-sim appends `###STOP###` inside its confirmation turn, ending the episode before the agent can act. Three iterations each had to re-derive this from traces. If the harness can detect "episode ended on a user turn that also carried the confirmation," marking those trials as agent-uncontrollable would stop optimizers from burning budget on prose anti-STALL rules the SKILL already refutes.
